roles.dev_title: Project 1: System Development for a Japanese Client in the Aviation Industry
roles.dev_p1: Worked in a 6-member team entrusted by the client with end-to-end Waterfall development (Basic Design → Detail Design → PG → UT → FT → ST → UAT); responsible for Detail Design, PG, UT and FT.
roles.dev_p2: Developed the backend server (C++, Makefile, PostgreSQL), desktop client UI (Visual Basic, GrapeCity Spread / InputMan) and web UI (Java, HTML/CSS), communicating via WebSocket.
roles.dev_p3: Supported task progress reporting to the Japanese client in Japanese at weekly meetings.
roles.ai_title: Project 2 (in parallel, client-requested): AI-Driven Development Automation
roles.ai_p1: Researched and introduced Devin AI to the team, building a framework that generates detail design documents and source code for the backend server, web UI and Visual Basic client.
roles.ai_p2: Designed the framework to reduce AI hallucination and keep the output consistent with project standards.
roles.ai_p3: Cut Detail Design + PG time for complex tasks from ~10 to ~4 days (including review), reducing effort by ~60%.
roles.lead_p1: Helped establish the process for a newly formed team, creating Detail Design, PG, UT and FT checklists that eliminated recurring mistakes such as document formatting errors and missed precondition checks before testing.
roles.lead_p2: Drafted task estimates and WBS, identifying and factoring in hidden effort such as meetings, repeated review-fix rounds and partial allocation (e.g., 0.8 instead of 1.0).
roles.lead_p3: Discovered that members' hidden overtime came from estimates omitting effort for two review rounds; confirmed the same issue in other sub-teams and proposed a team-wide fix to the estimation process, noticeably reducing hidden overtime on subsequent tasks.
roles.lead_p4: Managed the progress of 1–2 members with no missed deadlines, and supported the PM in reporting the team's overall progress to the client.
